items.rule: The coordinates of point P(x,y) dividing AB joining A(x1,y1) and B(x2,y2) internally in ratio m1:m2 are found by a cross-weighted average.
items.example: For A(-1,7), B(4,-3), ratio 2:3 gives P(1,3).

items.rule: The centroid is the average of the three vertex coordinates.
items.example: Average all three x-coordinates and all three y-coordinates separately.

items.example: Clear the denominator and isolate the missing endpoint coordinate.

concepts.title: 1. Section Formula for Internal Division
concepts.subtitle: Finding the coordinates of a division point
concepts.summary: The section formula gives the coordinates of a point P that divides the segment joining two endpoints internally in a specified ratio.

points.text: Multiply m₁ with the coordinates of B and m₂ with the coordinates of A.
Divide each weighted coordinate sum by m₁ + m₂.

concepts.subtitle: Average the three vertex coordinates
concepts.summary: The centroid is obtained by averaging the three x-coordinates and independently averaging the three y-coordinates.

points.text: Add x₁ + x₂ + x₃ and divide by 3.
Add y₁ + y₂ + y₃ and divide by 3.
Combine the two coordinate averages into G.
